beats.text: What is softer than water? You can scatter it with a hand, pour it, step through it.
Yet water carves canyons out of stone. Given time, nothing hard can resist it.
"The softest thing in the world overcomes the hardest," Lao Tzu wrote in the Tao Te Ching.
He called the way of water wu wei — action without forcing, moving with the grain of things.
Not laziness. Not giving up. Water never stops — it simply never fights the shape of the land.
We exhaust ourselves pushing against walls. The Tao says: flow around them instead.
Be like water. Yield, persist, and in the end wear the mountain down.

source_note: Quote: Tao Te Ching, trans. James Legge (1891, public domain).
